thread.title: Dow Jones Whipsaws Lower; Jobs Report, OPEC Meeting, Huawei CFO Arrest: Weekly Review |

author: IBD STAFF
title: Dow Jones Whipsaws Lower; Jobs Report, OPEC Meeting, Huawei CFO Arrest: Weekly Review |
text:
The Dow Jones and other major averages rallied Monday after the Trump-Xi meeting, but stocks and bond yields then fell sharply in whipsaw fashion, ending the week with big losses. The arrest of Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou raised China trade truce doubts. Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ), Dollar General ( DG ) and several retailers gave disappointing holiday outlooks, while software earnings were strong. The OPEC meeting ended with a crude oil production cut. A tame jobs report gives policymakers more flexibility on Fed rate hikes. Tobacco giant Altria ( MO ) agreed to buy 45% of Canadian cannabis producer Cronos Group ( CRON ).
Stocks Whipsaw Lower, Treasury Yields Dive The Dow Jones, S&P 500 and the Nasdaq composite all fell more than 4.5% for the week. China trade truce hopes quickly soured, with President Donald Trump touting himself as "Tariff Man" and Huawei CFO Wanzhou arrested. Treasury yields fell sharply, with the yield curve partially inverting. Ulta Beauty, Dollar General, Five Below ( FIVE ) and, to some extent, Lululemon ( LULU ) disappointed with holiday-quarter guidance, joining several other retailers. Software makers continued to deliver strong earnings results. Crude oil prices rebounded as the OPEC meeting ended with a production cut deal. November job growth cooled and wage gains were slightly below views, offering policymakers more reason to go slow on Fed rate hikes.
Jobs Report Shows Softer Side The U.S. added 155,000 jobs in November, fewer than expected, while growth failed to accelerate from the 3.1% nine-year high notched a month earlier. Unemployment held at a 49-year low 3.7% for a third straight month. The jobs report didn't have the kind of sizzle that would force policymakers to question their nascent dovish shift on Fed rate hikes. The IBD/TIPP Economic Optimism Index matched its lowest level of the year in early December, a still moderately optimistic 52.6, but the six-month economic outlook gauge fell below the neutral 50 level to the most pessimistic reading of the Trump era.
Yet the Institute for Supply Management's manufacturing survey index came in well above expectations at a robust 59.3, boosted by strength in new orders. The ISM nonmanufacturing index left estimates in the dust, rising to a lofty 60.7.
OPEC, Russia Agree To Crude Oil Production Cut After a two-day meeting in Vienna, OPEC and top nonmembers agreed to cut output by 1.2 million barrels per day in an effort to support oil prices. Under the deal, OPEC will cut 0.8 million bpd with Russia and other nonmembers accounting for the rest. Crude oil prices rallied Friday, but are near 2018 lows. Analysts say the cut isn't enough as Saudi Arabia and others were producing at record highs and economists are worried about a global economic slowdown in 2019. The U.S. has become a net exporter for the first time in 75 years. The Energy Information Administration said U.S. oil stockpiles fell by 7.3 million barrels, snapping 10 weeks of increases.
Discount Retailers See Weak Holiday Season Dollar General, closeout specialist Ollie's Bargain Outlet ( OLLI ) and teen-focused Five Below all reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings. But all three highly rated discount retailers gave mixed-to-weak guidance for the holiday quarter. That follows weak holiday guidance from off-price leaders Ross Stores ( ROST ) and TJX ( TJX ). All three stock suffered big losses
Software Earnings Strong Several software makers reported strong results and guidance. Software stocks generally rallied on the post-earnings day, but ended the week slightly higher or lower.
Cybersecurity firm Okta ( OKTA ) reported a narrower-than-expected Q3 loss as revenue rose 58% to $105.6 million. The security software maker, which provides identity management services, is signing up larger customers, analysts said. Okta also gave strong guidance. Zscaler ( ZS ), a cloud cybersecurity provider, said third quarter revenue jumped 59% to $63.3 million as it unexpectedly earned 1 cent a share ex items, its first profitable quarter. Sales and marketing costs decelerated for the fourth straight quarter. Free cash flow increased for the third quarter in a row.
MongoDB ( MDB ) reported a narrower-than-expected Q3 loss as revenue topped analyst estimates. The database software company said it lost 30 cents a share vs. 44 cents a year ago, with revenue rising 57% to $65 million. Analysts expected a loss of 40 cents a share on sales of $60.25 million. For the current quarter, MongoDB estimated revenue of $73.5 million. That topped consensus estimates of $64.7 million.
Coupa Software ( COUP ) unexpectedly swung to an adjusted Q3 profit with revenue topping expectations. The spending management software maker expects to break even on an adjusted basis for the current quarter, above views.
Smartsheet ( SMAR ) reported a narrower-than-expected Q3 loss as revenue jumped 59% to nearly $47 million, topping estimates of $44.2 million. The maker of project management software raised fiscal 2019 billings guidance to about $211 million
Cloudera ( CLDR ), which has agreed to merge with Hortonworks ( HDP ), reported a narrower-than-expected Q3 loss as revenue topped estimates. Cloudera stock popped Thursday but closed the week slightly lower, though analysts worry customer acquisition could slow pending the merger.
Lululemon Earnings Strong, But Not Enough Popular yogawear maker Lululemon ( LULU ) grew Q3 profit 34% to 75 cents a share and revenue by 21% to $748 million. Both beat views, though they snapped several quarters of accelerating growth. Total comparable sales rose 17%, well ahead of views. Direct-to-consumer revenue rose 44%. For the current holiday quarter, Lululemon guided for $1.64-$1.67 in EPS and $1.115 billion-$1.1125 billion in revenue, the midpoints of which are slightly above consensus, per Zacks estimates. The results and outlook didn't satisfy investors, with shares plunging 13% Friday.
Ulta Beauty Holiday Guidance Not So Pretty Ulta Beauty Q3 earnings rose 28% to $2.18 per share, beating views by 2 cents, as net sales grew 16% to $1.56 billion, matching estimates. Comparable store sales at the specialty beauty retailer rose 7.8%, in line with views. Retail comps also met projections with 4.4% growth. But Ulta Beauty guidance for the crucial holiday quarter was below consensus, sending shares crashing 13% Friday.
Auto Sales Downshift U.S. auto sales fell to a seasonally adjusted annualized rate of 17.4 million in November vs. 17.6 million in October and in November 2017. Ford Motor ( F ) saw sales shrink 6.9%, a smaller-than-expected decline. Nissan ( NSANY ) and Honda Motor ( HMC ) sales saw double-digit drops. Bucking the trend, Fiat Chrysler ( FCAU ) saw sales soar 17% on robust Jeep demand; the automaker later said it'll reopen a Detroit factory to make SUVs. The Big 3 auto stocks — Ford, Fiat Chrysler and General Motors ( GM ) — fell broadly on the week, as President Trump backpedaled on his claim of an "incredible" China trade deal rolling back auto tariffs. Meanwhile, GM CEO Mary Barra took heat on Capitol Hill over plans for factory closures and mass layoffs. She called her meetings with lawmakers "very constructive," without backing down.
Altria Will Buy 45% Of Marijuana Stock Cronos Tobacco giant Altria ( MO ) will pay $1.8 billion for 45% of Canadian cannabis company Cronos Group ( CRON ), which soared 39%. Altria announced it will discontinue some e-cigarette and oral nicotine products. The Altria-Cronos deal follows a big investment by Corona beer maker Constellation Brands ( STZ ) in marijuana play Canopy Growth ( CGC ). Cronos and Canopy rival Aphria ( APHA ) plunged after two short-seller reports claimed that acquisitions in Latin America, Jamaica and Florida were orchestrated to enrich insiders as ownership of companies there passed from shell companies and, eventually, onto Aphria. Shares lost nearly half their value before rebounding late in the week.
Delta Air, Hawaiian Sink Airlines Delta Air Lines ( DAL ) dragged legacy rivals United Airlines ( UAL ) and American Airlines ( AAL ) lower after the carrier cut its fourth-quarter unit revenue forecast. Still, Delta expects earnings per share to come in at the upper end of its outlook for $1.10-$1.30. Delta also said it was "on track" to grow pretax margins during the quarter, as fuel-price increases ease and it reins in other costs. Hawaiian Airlines parent Hawaiian Holdings ( HA ) also cut its Q4 unit revenue outlook as demand slows. Southwest Airlines ( LUV ) reported capacity growth outstripped traffic gains in November.
Apple iPhone Purchase Plans Drop Apple ( AAPL ) stock fell amid fresh reports of weakening iPhone sales. In the U.S., iPhone purchase intent has dropped to a five-year low as consumers hold on to their existing handsets for longer, a UBS survey indicated. Also, more consumers are opting to buy less-expensive, older-model iPhones, UBS said. Broadcom ( AVGO ) also said older iPhones were popular. The Apple chipmaker beat estimates for its fiscal fourth quarter and raised its sales guidance for fiscal 2019. It also increased its dividend by 51%. Audio-chip maker Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ) joined iPhone component suppliers warning of weak December quarter results as iPhone production slows. HSBC downgraded Apple to hold, saying hardware unit growth is "over for now." Morgan Stanley cut its Apple price target, citing weaker demand in China.
Drug News GlaxoSmithKline ( GSK ) on Monday announced a $5.1 billion plan to acquire Tesaro ( TSRO ), sending shares up 59%. Also Monday, Biohaven Pharmaceutical ( BHVN ) jumped more than 25% on a Phase 3 study of its acute migraine treatment. At the two-hour mark, 21.2% and 35.1% of patients were pain-free or experienced relief from their most bothersome symptoms, respectively, vs. just 10.9% and 26.8% of patients who received the placebo. Vanda Pharmaceuticals ( VNDA ) spiked nearly 26% on Monday after its gastroparesis drug increased the number of nausea-free days for patients by 28.8% vs. 15% for the placebo group. On Tuesday, Clovis Oncology ( CLVS ) rose 4.8% after the European Commission upheld Clovis' patent covering several crystalline forms of rucaparib camsylate, the drug name for ovarian cancer drug Rubraca.
News In Brief Edwards Lifesciences ( EW ) guided to 11%-15% sales growth in transcatheter heart-valve replacements for 2019. The medtech sees total revenue rising 9%-12% on an underlying basis.
HealthEquity ( HQY ) reported better-than-expected earnings and revenue, though top-line growth decelerated modestly for a fourth straight quarter. The health savings account custodian raised full-year guidance, but still below analyst views. Shares plunged.
Nexstar ( NXST ) will buy Tribune Media ( TRCO ) for $6.4 billion, including debt, which will make Nexstar the largest local TV station operator. Nexstar reportedly outbid private equity firm Apollo Global Management ( APO ). Tribune had backed out of a takeover deal by Sinclair Broadcasting ( SBGI ) amid regulator objections.
Chip-equipment maker Lam Research ( LRCX ) replaced CEO Martin Anstice amid an investigation of alleged workplace misconduct. It's the fourth chip company to oust its CEO for misconduct this year, following departures at Intel ( INTC ), Texas Instruments ( TXN ) and Rambus ( RMBS ).
Chip-design software maker Synopsys ( SNPS ) met Wall Street's estimates for earnings in its fiscal fourth quarter while sales beat views. Its sales and earnings guidance for the current quarter were below views.
Momo ( MOMO ), one of China's top mobile social networking platforms, matched Wall Street's target for earnings in the third quarter on better-than-expected revenue. But Momo gave weak guidance for the December quarter.
Grocery store giant Kroger ( KR ) topped earnings views but same-store sales growth just missed views.
